title: Sorcha nic Dhùghaill buys a launch's engine at Ros dhomhain
summary: Sorcha nic Dhùghaill, boatwright of Caol fhiadhaich, finds in a chandler's yard behind the coal quay at Ros dhomhain the engine of a harbour launch, laid up eight years because its coal cost more than the launch earned. She buys it for the price of old iron, and it is carried down the coast road to her yard on an ox-wain.

title: The smith of Caol fhiadhaich makes a dubhan burner
summary: Seonaidh Bàn, smith of the harbour at Caol fhiadhaich, makes a burner of iron with a pipe and a cock to feed dubhan to the engine in Sorcha nic Dhùghaill's rope-shed. He copies it from the stove of a coaster out of Seann Skell on the southern coast, made larger. The south-coast boats have burned dubhan in their stoves and lamps since the works' first year.

title: The keel of An Ròn Dubh bored
summary: At the asking of her skipper Lachann mac Neacail, Sorcha nic Dhùghaill hauls the decked boat An Ròn Dubh up her slip at Caol fhiadhaich and bores the sternpost and deadwood below the water for a shaft, against the guild's first rule, Cha tollar an druim. The other three yards of the town watch from the head of the slip.

title: An Ròn Dubh crosses the harbour under engine
summary: On a calm evening of an Lùnastal the fishing boat An Ròn Dubh, her engine fed by dubhan, crosses the harbour of Caol fhiadhaich to the wolf-stone and back with her sails furled and her oars shipped. Half the town watches from the wall. It is the first fishing boat of the island moved by an engine.

title: The boatwrights of Caol fhiadhaich return their papers
summary: The four yards of Caol fhiadhaich meet in the net-loft over the fish-store, hear the master's letter read, and answer it in writing: they hold the work lawful and will go on with it, and since the guild holds it unlawful for its members, they are members no longer. Their papers of binding go back to Ros dhomhain with the letter.

title: Comann nan Saor-luinge strikes and fines the yards of Caol fhiadhaich
summary: Comann nan Saor-luinge strikes the four yards of Caol fhiadhaich from its roll and lays a fine on each, the heaviest on Sorcha nic Dhùghaill's yard. None of them pays. The maor of the shire, written to by the guild, answers that a guild's fine is the guild's business.

title: A pilot takes an engine-boat through the strait
summary: After the season's offering at the harbour wolf-stone, Ailig Mòr, eldest of the strait pilots of Caol fhiadhaich, takes An Ròn Dubh out through the skerries under her engine, the first hull the pilots have brought through the strait without sail or oar. At the second skerry she drives across the tide.

title: An Ròn Dubh comes home against a south-westerly
summary: Late in an Dàmhair a south-westerly gale catches the fleet of Caol fhiadhaich on the herring banks off the south coast. The sailing boats run for the lee of a headland to the east and lie there five days. Lachann mac Neacail brings An Ròn Dubh home into the wind under her engine and lands the only fresh herring on the coast, sold at Doire shean at dawn.

title: All four yards of Caol fhiadhaich fitting engines
summary: By an Dùbhlachd all four yards of Caol fhiadhaich are boring keels and fitting engines to the town's fishing boats, and there are more skippers asking than there are slips. Donnchadh Ruadh, the oldest boatwright of the town, fits his first engine before the year is out.

title: Three yards of the south-west coast follow
summary: In the first months of the year the yards of Inis chrom, Doire shean and a third harbour of the south-west coast send to Caol fhiadhaich to learn how the engines are fitted, and begin the same work. They too leave Comann nan Saor-luinge or are struck from it.

title: Launch engines dear at Ros dhomhain
summary: No one on the island makes engines for boats, and the yards of the south-west buy the engine out of every laid-up launch in the harbours of the capital country. The chandlers of Ros dhomhain, who sold such engines for old iron the summer before, ask three times the price by am Màrt and five times by an Giblean.

title: The guild summons the boatwrights of Caol fhiadhaich
summary: Early in an Giblean Comann nan Saor-luinge summons the boatwrights of Caol fhiadhaich to its court at Ros dhomhain to hear its ruling on the matter of the engines. The four yards send Sorcha nic Dhùghaill to answer for all of them.

title: Sorcha nic Dhùghaill declines readmission
summary: In the guild hall above the slips at Ros dhomhain, when the master Pàdraig mac an t-Saoir has read the ruling and remitted the fines, Sorcha nic Dhùghaill answers for the four yards of Caol fhiadhaich that they bored the keels as shipwrights and have no need of a shipwrights' guild that disowns the work. The clerk writes that they decline.

title: Cha tollar an druim
summary: The first rule of Comann nan Saor-luinge, the keel is not bored, is broken at Caol fhiadhaich when Sorcha nic Dhùghaill bores the post of An Ròn Dubh to take a shaft.

title: The pilots' word at the wolf-stone
summary: Ailig Mòr, eldest of the pilots of Caol fhiadhaich, says the words over the fish at the wolf-stone for the first engine-boat to go out, and then takes her through the strait himself.

title: The four yards return their papers
summary: The boatwrights of Caol fhiadhaich write to the master of their guild that they hold the engine work lawful, and return their papers with the letter. Sorcha nic Dhùghaill takes down her binding-paper from its frame.

title: The Seann Skell works watch the guild court
summary: A man sent from the dubhan works at the southern Seann Skell sits at the court of Comann nan Saor-luinge at Ros dhomhain beside a clerk of the lights, to hear what it says of engines.

title: An Ròn Dubh laid up for the winter
summary: The shaft-boat An Ròn Dubh is drawn up the slip at Caol fhiadhaich for the winter, and the shipwrights of the town come down one at a time to look at the bored post.
